source_user: Write a concise runbook entry for an engineer investigating prefill. Case variant 4: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Prefill processes the prompt and is generally parallel across prompt tokens; its cost is dominated by prompt processing and often compute utilization.
corrected_answer: Prefill is the initial forward pass over the input prompt before autoregressive decoding. Mechanism: attention and projection kernels process multiple prompt positions in parallel and materialize the initial K/V state that decode will read. Boundary condition: parallelism and cost depend on prompt length, padding, batch shape, precision, hardware, and prefix-cache reuse; a short prompt or cache hit may not show the same behavior. Record model and software versions and measure TTFT, prompt tokens/s, peak memory, utilization, and p95/p99 latency against a matched baseline; treat platform-specific performance as evidence-required.

source_assistant: Decode generates one or a few tokens per step and repeatedly reads model weights and KV state; it is often sensitive to memory bandwidth and scheduling.

source_user: Contrast continuous batching with a naive implementation that does not use it. Case variant 1: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Continuous batching admits and retires requests at iteration boundaries so completed sequences do not hold a static batch slot.
corrected_answer: Continuous batching dynamically admits requests and retires completed sequences at iteration boundaries, reusing available work slots instead of waiting for a fixed batch. A naive static batch holds completed slots until the whole batch ends, reducing utilization; continuous batching schedules active sequences each iteration. Boundary condition: admission, padding, scheduler overhead, fairness, and KV fragmentation can erase gains or increase tails. Compare identical tokenized workloads and limits, measuring TTFT, inter-token p99, prompt/output tokens/s, queueing, occupancy, memory, evictions, and errors.
